# Input

Generated from the spec. This page is a reference to the contract, not usage guidance.

A single-line text field with its label, an optional description and an error message, as one component.

Stage: **alpha**. Figma: `TextField` (mapping not yet confirmed against the Components file). Behaviour: plain HTML.

## Keyboard

Pattern: [W3C WAI Forms tutorial: labelling controls, form instructions and user notifications. There is no Authoring Practices pattern for a plain text field; the native input is used.](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/). Name: The label element, tied to the input by for and id. Without a visible label, the ariaLabel prop.

| Key | Part | Does | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tab | input | Moves focus into the field and on to the next one. A read-only field is reached; a disabled field is skipped. | `input-tab-order` |
| Shift+Tab | input | Moves focus to the previous field. | browser |
| Typing and text editing keys | input | Edits the value as the browser does. Nothing is overridden. | browser |
| Escape | input | With type search, some browsers clear the value. The component adds nothing. | browser |
| Enter | input | Submits the enclosing form, as the browser does. The component never stops it. | `input-enter-submits-form` |

| Level | Id | Requirement | Checked by | WCAG |

| MUST | `input-native-element` | The input part is an input element. It is never a div with contenteditable. | `test:input-native-element` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `input-label` | The input has an accessible name: a label element tied by for and id, or ariaLabel. | `axe:label` | 1.3.1 |
| MUST | `input-label-or-aria-label` | The type of the props requires label or ariaLabel, and the component warns in development when both are missing. | `type:input-label-or-aria-label` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `input-ids-generated` | Without an id prop the input gets a unique id from useId, and the label's for, the description's id and the error message's id are made from it. Two inputs on one page never share an id. | `test:input-ids-generated` |  |
| MUST | `input-described-by` | aria-describedby on the input lists the error message's id first while it is shown, then the description's id when there is one, and never an id that is not in the page. | `test:input-described-by` | 1.3.1 |
| MUST | `input-invalid-only-with-error` | aria-invalid is true on the input only while the error message is shown, and is absent otherwise. | `test:input-invalid-only-with-error` | 3.3.1 |
| MUST | `input-invalid-needs-message` | invalid without an errorMessage is a type error, and the component warns in development. | `type:input-invalid-needs-message` | 3.3.1 |
| MUST | `input-aria-valid` | Every ARIA attribute on the input holds a valid value. | `axe:aria-valid-attr-value` | 4.1.2 |
| MUST | `input-error-not-colour-alone` | An error is shown by words and an icon and a 2 pixel edge, never by colour alone. | `test:input-error-not-colour-alone` | 1.4.1 |
| MUST | `input-required-not-colour-alone` | A required field shows the word Required next to its label and sets the native required attribute. It is never marked by colour alone. | `test:input-required-not-colour-alone` | 3.3.2 |
| MUST | `input-tab-order` | Tab reaches the input when it is enabled or read-only and skips it when disabled. | `test:input-tab-order` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `input-enter-submits-form` | Enter in the input submits the enclosing form; the component does not cancel it. | `test:input-enter-submits-form` | 2.1.1 |
| MUST | `input-focus-visible` | While the input has focus the control shows a ring at least 2 pixels thick with at least 3 to 1 contrast against what is beside it, and the input shows no second outline of its own. | `test:input-focus-visible` | 2.4.7 |
| MUST | `input-edge-contrast` | The control's edge has at least 3 to 1 contrast against the page in every state except disabled, in light and dark. | `test:input-edge-contrast` | 1.4.11 |
| MUST | `input-text-contrast` | The value, label, description and error text have at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against their background in every state except disabled, in light and dark. | `axe:color-contrast` | 1.4.3 |
| MUST | `input-placeholder-contrast` | The placeholder has at least 4.5 to 1 contrast against the control's fill in light and dark. It fails in light today until the text/placeholder override lands. | `test:input-placeholder-contrast` | 1.4.3 |
| MUST | `input-no-ios-zoom` | Where the pointer is coarse the input's text is at least 16 pixels at every size, so iOS does not zoom the page on focus. (pattern) | `test:input-no-ios-zoom` |  |
| MUST | `input-target-size` | The control is at least 24 by 24 pixels at every size. | `test:input-target-size` | 2.5.8 |
| MUST | `input-reflow` | At 320 pixels wide and at 200 percent text size, nothing in the field is clipped or hidden: the control grows taller, and the label, description and error message wrap. | `test:input-reflow` | 1.4.10 |
| MUST | `input-text-resize` | With text at 200 percent the control is never shorter than its text; it uses a least height, not a fixed one. | `test:input-text-resize` | 1.4.4 |
| MUST | `input-field-stack` | The label, the control, the description and the error message stack top to bottom in that order, spaced by the root gap, and the error icon sits before the error words on their first line. | `test:input-field-stack` | 1.3.2 |
| MUST | `input-control-row` | The prefix, the input and the suffix sit on one row inside the control, centred vertically. The input takes the width that is left and may shrink; the prefix and suffix keep their size. At 320 pixels wide the typed text never runs under the prefix or the suffix. | `test:input-control-row` | 1.4.10 |
| MUST | `input-decorations-hidden` | The prefix, the suffix, the required mark and the error icon carry aria-hidden. | `test:input-decorations-hidden` | 1.1.1 |
| MUST | `input-autocomplete-valid` | A field that collects the person's own details sets a valid autocomplete token. | `axe:autocomplete-valid` | 1.3.5 |
| MUST | `input-placeholder-not-label` | The placeholder is never the only label or the only instruction; it disappears as soon as the person types. (pattern) | `manual:input-placeholder-not-label` | 3.3.2 |
| SHOULD | `input-touch-target` | Where the pointer is coarse the control is at least 44 pixels tall. (pattern) | `test:input-touch-target` |  |

| SHOULD | `input-no-number-for-codes` | Amounts, card numbers, postal codes and one-time codes use type text with inputMode numeric or decimal, not type number, which changes the value on scroll, drops leading zeros and is read poorly by some screen readers. (pattern) | `manual:input-no-number-for-codes` |  |

| COULD | `input-required-word-understood` | People understand the word Required next to a label faster than an asterisk explained elsewhere on the page. (assumption) | `manual:input-required-word-understood` |  |

## Content rules

- The label names the value in a few words, in sentence case, with no colon and no full stop: Email address, not Email:.
- The label carries any meaning shown by the prefix or suffix: Amount in dollars, not Amount with a dollar sign beside it.
- The description gives the format or why the value is asked for, in one sentence.
- The error message says what is wrong and how to fix it, in one sentence, without blame: Enter a postal code with 5 digits, not Invalid input.
- The placeholder is an example of a value, never an instruction and never the label.
- Required fields show the word Required. When most fields in a form are required, the form may instead mark the few optional ones with the word Optional, and says so at the top.

## What the spec does not carry

- The live Figma components: their properties were read from a cached copy inside the Semantic Tokens file, which is older than the published library, so every figma mapping here is unconfirmed. That copy has two components. Input, the bare control, has variant (primary, secondary), state (placeholder, hover, focus, filled, error, disabled), type (text, password, number) and a text property value. TextField wraps Input and adds the label and description, with the same six state values, the booleans showLabel and showDescription and the instance swap typeInput. This spec covers what Figma calls TextField.
- The code component was called InputField and is renamed Input. That name was never a Figma name, so it is not recorded in the figma block.
- Figma's variant property on Input, with the values primary and secondary: what each looks like could not be read, so the spec has no variant prop. One look is specified until the two can be compared.
- Figma's type list (text, password, number) is shorter than the spec's; email, search, tel and url exist in code only.
- showLabel and showDescription: design-tool switches that code does not need. Pass the label or the description, or leave it out. The typeInput instance swap likewise has no prop: the code renders its own input part.
- Read-only has no Figma state value; the readOnly state exists in code only.
- Layout written in the extensions stylesheet: the root is a column (which is what makes its gap work); the control is a row with its items centred vertically; the input takes the leftover width and may shrink while the prefix and suffix do not; the error message is a row with the icon first. Proven by input-field-stack and input-control-row, not by styles.
- The icon set: prefix, suffix and the error icon take an icon node, but no Icon component spec exists yet.
- Validation logic and when to run it: the product decides when invalid becomes true.
- Moving focus to the first invalid field after a failed submit, and an error summary at the top of the form: these belong to a Form component.
- A multi-line text area, a select, a combobox, a date field and a field with a clear or show-password button inside it.
- Character counters and maxLength guidance.
- Other native attributes such as maxLength, pattern, min, max and onBlur: they pass through to the input unchanged and have no styles.
- A success or warning state for the field.
- Forced-colours mode beyond what the browser does to borders and outlines.
- Motion beyond a colour transition on the control.
